question: The Commission’s Joint Research Centre has highlighted the importance of access to in-vehicle data and functions for the competitiveness of the European automotive aftermarket1. However, fair access to in-vehicle data and functions for safer, smarter, and more affordable mobility is being hindered by the absence of an European in-vehicle data regulation.

The Commission has decided to address this issue with a legislative proposal on access to in-vehicle data, functions, and resources. However, although the publication of the proposal is still listed for the second quarter of 2023, there has been no update on the state of the proposal. In this context: 1.
What is the current state of the proposal on access to in-vehicle data, functions and resources?
Will the proposal still be published before the end of this mandate?
Has the Commission explored the possibility of addressing market imbalances that are partly caused by the considerable delay to the proposal?
Joint Research Centre, Access to digital car data and competition in aftersales services, JRC Digital Economy Working Paper 2018-06, September 2018.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.5.2024) As announced in the European Data Strategy1, the Commission fully recognises the importance of strengthening the data economy. Notably, the Commission adopted, in February 2022, a proposal for the Data Act2 (adopted by the co-legislator in 2023) and, in November 2023, the Communication on the creation of the common European mobility data space3.

The Data Act, on its own, can be expected to significantly improve the capacity of the European consumers and businesses to maximise benefits from the data generated by all connected devices, including vehicle data.

The Commission also sees the potential of improved access to vehicle data, functions and resources to stimulate the development of connected vehicle services, ensuring competition, boosting competitiveness of the European automotive ecosystem and preserving safety and security for the users.

Therefore, the Commission services have been working on a sectorspecific legislative proposal on access to vehicle data, functions and resources, on which significant progress has been made. However, considering the expected complexity of the ensuing legislative process and the upcoming parliamentary recess, it was deemed advisable not to table the proposal at this stage of the mandate.

In the meantime, the Commission has started preparations on a delegated act under the TypeApproval Framework Regulation for motor vehicles4, with a view to clarifying essential aspects related to access to repair and maintenance information and give certainty to all stakeholders, including independent aftermarket operators.
